name: Science
topics: Living things · Food chains · Plants · Habitats · Life cycles · States of matter · Human body

licoes.texto: A food chain shows how energy passes from one living thing to another. It always starts with the Sun.
pontos: Producers (plants) make their own food with sunlight.
Herbivores eat only plants. Carnivores eat only meat. Omnivores eat both.
Decomposers (fungi and bacteria) break down dead plants and animals.
grass → rabbit → fox
licoes.fala: I eat rice, beans and chicken, so I am an omnivore!

licoes.texto: Each part of a plant has a job.
pontos: Roots take in water and hold the plant in the soil.
Stem carries water up and holds the plant up.
Leaves make food by photosynthesis: sunlight + water + carbon dioxide → food + oxygen.
Flowers make seeds; fruits protect the seeds.
licoes.fala: Plants give us the oxygen we breathe. Thank you, plants!

licoes.texto: A habitat is the home of a living thing. An adaptation is a special feature that helps it survive there.
pontos: Desert: a cactus stores water in its thick stem; a camel can go days without drinking.
Arctic: a polar bear has thick fur and fat to stay warm.
Ocean: fish breathe with gills.
Rainforest: monkeys have long tails and arms to climb trees.
licoes.fala: If a polar bear lived in the desert, it would be way too hot! Every animal fits its habitat.

licoes.texto: A life cycle shows how a living thing is born, grows and makes new living things.
pontos: Butterfly: egg → caterpillar (larva) → chrysalis (pupa) → adult butterfly.
Frog: egg → tadpole → froglet → adult frog.
This big change in body shape is called metamorphosis.
licoes.fala: A tadpole has a tail and lives in water. Later it becomes a frog that jumps on land!

licoes.texto: Matter can be a solid (ice), a liquid (water) or a gas (water vapor).
pontos: Melting: solid → liquid (ice cream melts).
Freezing: liquid → solid (water becomes ice).
Evaporation: liquid → gas (puddles dry in the sun).
Condensation: gas → liquid (drops on a cold glass).
licoes.fala: My ice cream melted in the sun: solid to liquid. Science happens even at snack time!

licoes.texto: Our body has organs that work together in systems.
pontos: Heart: pumps blood around the body.
Lungs: help us breathe (take in oxygen).
Stomach: helps digest food.
Brain: controls the body. The skull protects it.
The skeleton holds us up and protects our organs.
licoes.fala: When I run, my heart beats faster to send more blood to my muscles!

licoes.texto: Microorganisms are living things so small that we need a microscope to see them.
pontos: Bacteria and fungi are examples.
Some are helpful: yeast makes bread rise; bacteria help make yogurt.
Some make us sick: wash your hands with soap and water for 20 seconds!
licoes.fala: Under the microscope, a drop of pond water is full of tiny living things!

questions.q: Which one is a living thing?
questions.fb: A tree grows, needs water and air, and makes new trees (seeds). Rocks, chairs and water are non-living.

questions.q: Plants are called producers because they...
opts: make their own food using sunlight
questions.fb: Plants produce their own food by photosynthesis. (Produtores.)

questions.q: In the food chain grass → rabbit → fox, the rabbit is a...
questions.fb: The rabbit eats the grass (a plant), so it is a herbivore, the first consumer.

questions.q: An animal that eats only meat is a...
questions.fb: Carnivores eat meat. Herbivores eat plants. Omnivores eat both.

questions.q: Humans eat plants and meat, so we are...
questions.fb: Omnivores eat both plants and animals.

questions.q: Mushrooms and bacteria that break down dead leaves are...
questions.fb: Decomposers break down dead things and return nutrients to the soil.

questions.q: Where does the energy in a food chain start?
questions.fb: Plants use the Sun's energy to make food. Then the energy passes to the animals.

questions.q: Which part of the plant takes in water from the soil?
questions.fb: Roots take in water and nutrients and hold the plant in the soil.

questions.q: Photosynthesis happens mainly in the...
questions.fb: Leaves capture sunlight to make food.

questions.q: During photosynthesis, plants release a gas that we need to breathe:
questions.fb: Plants take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen.

questions.q: A cactus can live in the desert because it...
opts: stores water in its thick stem
questions.fb: Storing water is an adaptation to the dry desert.

questions.q: A polar bear has thick fur and fat to...
opts: stay warm in the cold Arctic
questions.fb: Thick fur and fat keep the polar bear warm in the freezing Arctic.

questions.q: A special feature that helps a living thing survive in its habitat is called...
questions.fb: Adaptations are features or behaviors that help living things survive. (Adaptação.)

questions.q: Fish breathe under water using their...
questions.fb: Gills take oxygen from the water. (Brânquias.)

questions.q: What is the correct order of a butterfly's life cycle?
questions.fb: Egg → caterpillar (larva) → chrysalis (pupa) → butterfly.

questions.q: A baby frog that lives in water and has a tail is a...
questions.fb: A tadpole (girino) lives in water. Later it grows legs and loses its tail.

questions.q: The big change in body shape of a frog or a butterfly is called...
questions.fb: Metamorphosis is a big change in body shape during the life cycle.

questions.q: Ice is water in the ___ state.
questions.fb: Ice keeps its own shape: it is solid.

questions.q: When ice cream melts, it changes from...
questions.fb: Melting: solid → liquid.

questions.q: Bia noticed that puddles disappear on a sunny day. That happens because the water...
questions.fb: The Sun heats the water and it evaporates: liquid → gas (water vapor).

questions.q: Drops of water appear on the outside of a cold glass. This is...
questions.fb: Water vapor in the air touches the cold glass and turns into liquid: condensation.

questions.q: Which organ pumps blood around the body?
questions.fb: The heart is a muscle that pumps blood all the time.

questions.q: We use our lungs to...
questions.fb: The lungs take in oxygen when we breathe in.

questions.q: The skull protects the...
questions.fb: The skull (crânio) is a strong bone that protects the brain.

questions.q: Nico looked at pond water under a microscope and saw tiny living things. They are called...
questions.fb: Microorganisms are living things too small to see without a microscope.

questions.q: Which microorganism helps make bread rise?
questions.fb: Yeast is a tiny fungus. It makes gas bubbles that make the dough rise.

questions.q: What is the best way to remove germs from your hands?
opts: Wash with soap and water for 20 seconds
questions.fb: Soap and water for about 20 seconds removes most germs.
